about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.name: Abrams Sanitary District 1
channels.legal_basis: s. NR 210.21(5), Wis. Adm. Code, as the DNR's form 3400-184 instructions give it: "All overflows (SSOs & TFOs) are required to be public noticed according to s. NR 210.21(5), Wis. Adm. Code. Notification shall occur according to a facility's emergency response plan in their CMOM and occur promptly after any overflow event. ... At a minimum, if an overflow is to a surface water, a daily newspaper of general circulation shall be notified."
channels.note: Abrams Sanitary District 1 gives notice of an overflow by its emergency response plan; the DNR's minimum is a notice to a daily newspaper, which does not by itself say whether the notice reaches the web, and its report to the DNR is not published (wi-dnr-switchboard-sso-reports). Its own web channel was not searched individually.

NR 210.21(5), Wis. Adm. Code. Notification shall occur according to a facility's emergency response plan in their CMOM and occur promptly after any overflow event. ... At a minimum, if an overflow is to a surface water, a daily newspaper of general circulation shall be notified."
channels.note: City of Niagara gives notice of an overflow by its emergency response plan; the DNR's minimum is a notice to a daily newspaper, which does not by itself say whether the notice reaches the web, and its report to the DNR is not published (wi-dnr-switchboard-sso-reports). NR 210.21(5), Wis. Adm. Code. Notification shall occur according to a facility's emergency response plan in their CMOM and occur promptly after any overflow event. ... At a minimum, if an overflow is to a surface water, a daily newspaper of general circulation shall be notified."
channels.note: Ellsworth Wastewater Treatment gives notice of an overflow by its emergency response plan; the DNR's minimum is a notice to a daily newspaper, which does not by itself say whether the notice reaches the web, and its report to the DNR is not published (wi-dnr-switchboard-sso-reports). Its own web channel was not searched individually.

NR 210.21(5), Wis. Adm. Code. Notification shall occur according to a facility's emergency response plan in their CMOM and occur promptly after any overflow event. ... At a minimum, if an overflow is to a surface water, a daily newspaper of general circulation shall be notified."
